mechanism_narrative: A sustained 5-month decline in the GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls below 2% and remains below for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC exceeds 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of declining GDPC1 are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 3% signals accelerating supply-side growth, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises above 3% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC exceeds 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of rising INDPRO are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 2% and remains below for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC exceeds 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% signals labor market weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.

failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC exceeds 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of rising UNRATE are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
